g.text: Reproducible spike sorting on archived data
DANDI Compute takes an asset already in the archive, runs it through an established spike-sorting pipeline
on institutional compute, and returns the results as a new, versioned derivative Dandiset.
Hundreds of TB of raw extracellular
Decides what job to run on selected assets, using
The containerized AIND Ephys pipeline runs on
Sorted units, metrics and QC figures are saved
Four responsibilities, each deliberately small. The infrastructure never touches the science — it decides what to run, and makes sure the record of that decision survives.
Point at an asset. Pick a named set of pipeline
parameters and a compute profile, and write
out everything needed to run it.
Prepared jobs pile up on disk, one self-
contained bundle per asset. Nothing has run
yet, so anything can still be pruned or rebuilt.
The bundle is handed to an institutional cluster,
where the pipeline claims a different slice of
hardware for each of its steps.
Results, logs and the exact code are packaged
as a versioned derivative and pushed back out

Because the parameter set and the compute profile are both named, referenced things rather than typed-in flags, two runs that claim to be the same run really are (and two runs that differ say so in their identity).
A dispatch step fans the session out into one independent job per probe, shank and segment; the heavy work happens in parallel; the results are gathered back together at the end.
one job per probe · shank · segment
Parallelizing steps 2–6 makes the run affordable: only the sorting step needs a GPU, and only for one probe. Pipeline after
The output is a path you can read. Every level of the directory answers one question about where a result came from — nothing about the run is implicit, and nothing has to be looked up elsewhere.
Re-run with different parameters and you get a sibling directory, not an overwrite — the old result stays where it was.
The exact code that produced this, not just a reference to it.
What the run actually did, step by step.
Sorted units, waveforms and quality metrics.
QC figures, viewable straight from the browser.
Machine-readable provenance for the whole run.
Each run directory stands on its own — enough to check the result and reproduce it.
The derivative sits alongside the data it came from, so the result and its inputs stay connected.
